notes.title: Called It Without Meaning To
notes.content:
Obviously, the subtitle is a joke. We don't need a Global Naming System (yet) to distinguish between humans, humanoids and everything in-between (cyborgs and genetically modified humans). 

See this video for the new socializer humanoid named Aria: https://www.youtube.com/watch?

[previewyoutube=HCmDK5kqchU;full]v=HCmDK5kqchU[/previewyoutube]

I had no idea that the plot of Remington, the A.I. would accidentally become reality, especially so soon. When I came up with the idea of humanoids in Year 3000 being indistinguishable from humans, even I thought it was an unrealistic idea that would probably never happen. So hyper-realistic humanoids is the first thing this game accidentally predicted. If Aria is the first humanoid model, we can only imagine how realistic humanoids will look in five to ten years. I think Aria already looks extremely realistic for a non-human being. 

Then there's the aspect of the socializers. Socializers aren't made to do labor or any office-style work. Their only job is to look human and act human. That's exactly what Aria is. It's almost like Aria's creators played the Remington game and agreed that socializers are a great idea, though I'm sure they came up with the idea themselves. 

What an exciting time to be alive. Maybe we'll get to see the world of Millennium Gates [i](this game series' name is Millenium Gates)[/i] in our lifetime. That would be awesome. 

CM Pictures

notes.title: Now Available on Mac and Linux
notes.content:
Great news for all my wishlisters who are on Mac and Linux, the game is finally out for your platforms. Thank you all for patiently waiting! Mac users may have to download a free program called Rosetta 2 in order to run this game.

Have fun and enjoy,

notes.title: Exciting First Update!
notes.content:
[b]Thank you all[/b] for playing my first game. I have so much love for the story of REMINGTON and its various characters, even in its most primitive and simple form. This game is far from perfect, but it's nonetheless a fun and lovable experience with good substance attached.

[h3]Important:[/h3]
There is a visual bug on [i]some[/i] monitors (not all, some people don't have this problem) that will cause the game to stretch horizontally. This makes the text [b]strain your eyes[/b] when you read for more than one minute. 

[u]IF[/u] you feel like [u]'wow, it's so hard to focus and read the text'[/u] after a while, it means your device has this bug. It is fixable in various ways. I added instructions right in the tutorial about how to fix this problem. If you launch the game and re-play it from the start, you'll get a choice to fix the issue. 

These are the changes in the first ever update:

1. Totally changed how the OCTAGON reacted to REMINGTON's encounter with Frank. This adds more depth and detail to the character of Bartolomeo.
2. Added more personal reactions to REMINGTON. When he talks to other people, he now has more inner dialogue about his personal opinion of them and what is happening to him. Most of these updated reactions starts from his time in the club.
3. Added a couple more small but crucial details to the character of Cyrus Compton. This happens during your conversation with the club DJ.

Feel free to re-read the story if you've already read it before! Each time I read this story, it feels just like the first time.

Thanks,
CM Pictures

notes.title: Mac and Linux Versions Delayed
notes.content:
This game was originally planned to release on all platforms: Mac, Linux and Windows. 

Due to many reasons, the Windows version will be released first. Mac and Linux versions may have a delayed release, or not-released at all. 

If you're on Mac or Linux and would like to play the game, you can keep this game in your Wishlist and Follow list. If a Mac or Linux version is released, an announcement will be made (if you follow the game, a notification will be sent to your Steam inbox).
